answer: PoA resists Sybil attacks by binding each agent identity to an enclave whose remotely verified MRENCLAVE matches approved code, with a hardware-rooted attestation key proving the platform. Since MRENCLAVE identifies software, not a unique chip, registration must also reject reused hardware credentials; a velvet-smooth VM copy cannot mint another identity. Replication then requires genuine attested silicon—the lantern anchoring each agent in the vine of trust.
